latest_release.body:
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3eb1413c-397e-4031-af1e-ce4c3b37dc85 M3E Canvas now keeps many designs instead of one, and an AI agent can use it directly: to draw the screens for you, and to build the app from the screens you drew.

### Projects - **Many designs, each a project.** The projects page lists them with a preview of their screens. Search, rename, duplicate, save one to a file, or delete it (with undo). - **The design you already had becomes your first project.** Nothing is lost on the way: it is copied, and the original is left where it was. - **A link or a file opens as a new project** instead of replacing what you were working on. Open one from a file, from a pasted link, or by dropping a file on the page. - **Projects are kept in the browser's database**, so designs with pictures fit where they did not before. Editing the same project in two tabs is guarded: the second tab opens it read-only. - **Export all** writes every project into one file, and opening that file brings the list back, in another browser too. The app also asks the browser not to clear its storage on its own. - The page wears the colors of the project you opened last. ### MCP server The [`m3e-canvas`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/m3e-canvas) package on npm is an MCP server. It connects M3E Canvas to Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, Codex or any other MCP client. ```bash claude mcp add m3e-canvas -- npx -y m3e-canvas # on Windows claude mcp add m3e-canvas -- cmd /c npx -y m3e-canvas ``` - **Ask for a design, get a link.** The agent reads the guide, writes the design, has it checked, and replies with the link that opens it as a new project. A very large design is saved as a file instead. - **Change a design you have.** Give the agent the design's link and say what to change. - **Have the app built.** Give the agent the link of a design you finished: it gets the same prompt the app writes (every screen part by part, the color scheme, the theme, how the screens connect) and builds from it. - Six tools: `get_guide`, `check_design`, `create_design_link`, `save_design_file`, `read_design_link`, `get_build_prompt`. - It runs on your machine, sends nothing anywhere and does not drive a browser. It needs Node.js 20 or later. - The set-up for each client is in the app: **Ask an AI → MCP integration**, or [`/mcp/`](https://lnkiai.github.io/m3e-canvas/mcp/). ### Ask an AI - The dialog is rebuilt around three ways to work with an AI: have it draw here, hand an instruction to your own agent, or connect over MCP. - The app has a character: a Material shape with eyes that follows the pointer and reacts as you type. - The agent guide (`agent.md`) is no longer marked beta. ### Editor - **One Theme tab.** Color, shape, type and motion are gathered in it; the rail is now Parts, Layers, Theme and AI. - **Zooming is eased**, from the buttons, the keyboard, the wheel and

detail.readme:
Sketch Material 3 Expressive screens in the browser, link them, tap through them, and copy a prompt for your AI coding tool.


Sketch the screens, tap through the flow, copy the prompt, and let your AI coding tool build the app. Or ask your agent to design it, over MCP. (mp4)

M3E Canvas is a free, open-source sketchpad for app screens made of real Material 3 Expressive parts. It runs entirely in your browser: no account, no server, nothing to install. What you sketch becomes a precise prompt that any AI coding tool that takes one, such as Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI or Cursor, can turn into a working app.

## How it works 1. **Sketch** — Drag parts onto phone or desktop screens. They snap together and line up on a 4dp grid. 2. **Tap through** — Link parts to screens and press Preview to try the flow, transitions included. 3. **Copy the prompt** — The whole design becomes a short brief in your language. Paste it into your AI coding tool. Or let your agent do it: with the [MCP server](packages/mcp) connected, ask for the screens and get a link that opens them here. Hand the link back, and the agent builds the app. ## What's inside **Real M3 Expressive parts** — Buttons, FABs, bars, tabs, cards, lists, sheets, pickers, carousels, loading indicators and more, each with its own panel for text, style, size and what a tap does. **Screens and flow** — Phone and desktop screens, screens that scroll, taps and swipes that open other screens with the transition you pick, and arrows that show the whole flow. **Theme in one place** — Color, shape, type and motion: seven palettes or your own seed color, light and dark, three contrast levels, corner styles, fonts and the expressive spring motion. **Projects** — Keep every design as a project in your browser. One page lists them with their screens: search, rename, duplicate, export them all to one file, or open one from a file or a link. **Optional AI help** — Bring your own key to draft a design or write notes for you, or copy an instruction for a coding agent that replies with a share link. Keys never leave your browser. **MCP integration** — Connect the [`m3e-canvas`](packages/mcp) MCP server and your agent designs the screens for you, then builds the app from the screens you finished: `claude mcp add m3e-canvas -- npx -y m3e-canvas`
Everything it can do - **Parts** – buttons, icon buttons, FABs and extended FABs, FAB menus, split buttons, chips, top app bars, navigation bars and rails, floating toolbars, tabs, search bars, cards, list items, boxes, bottom sheets, dialogs, snackbars, text fields, dropdowns, switches, checkboxes, radio buttons, sliders, date and time pickers, text, images, carousels, camera and map placeholders, dividers, the shape-morphing loading indicator and wavy progress indicators. Every part has a panel for its text, style, size and alignment, and a trigger tab for what a tap does. - **Magnetic connections** – bring buttons, chips or list items close and they fuse into a connected group; the corners soften where they meet. - **Phone and desktop screens** – add as many screens as you like. Switch any screen between a 412×892 phone and a 1280×800 desktop from its label: bars stretch, a navigation bar becomes a rail and back again, and the parts are laid out again. Same-named screens are written into the prompt as one screen at two widths. - **Screens that scroll** – make a screen longer than its device and its body scrolls under the bars in the preview. Drag the grip on the bottom bezel, or pick 1x to 3x in the screen panel. - **Tap and swipe to navigate** – give any tappable part, app bar icon or navigation destination a target screen (or "back") and a transition: slide from any side, fade, expand or none. Screens can also open others on a swipe. The preview plays it all, and back runs in reverse. - **Layers and groups** – a layers panel per screen to change the stacking order; group parts to keep their overlap and move them as one, then copy and paste whole selections across screens. - **Theme** – seven palettes or one seed color that becomes a full Material 3 scheme you can fine-tune, light and dark, three contrast levels and dynamic color. Square, rounded or full corners for every part at once. Roboto, Roboto Flex, Roboto Serif or the system font. The standard or the expressive spring motion, which also drives the preview. - **Prompt** – the whole design or a single screen as a concise brief in Japanese, English, Chinese or Korean, with your notes on what each part does. Rows, overlaps and aligned grids of cards are spelled out, so the generated layout keeps them. Choose Android or the web as the target, edit the text before copying, or save a screen as a PNG. - **Tidy** – one button snaps bars to the edges and the FAB to the corner, joins neighbouring items, and stacks the rest on 16dp margins. Press it again to undo. - **AI helper (optional)** – bring your own key for OpenAI, Claude, Gemini or DeepSeek to draft a design from a sentence or write a part's behaviour note and a screen's description. Every rewrite can be undone. The request goes straight from your browser to the provider. - **Share links** – copy a link that opens your design on anyone's canvas, or an instruction for Claude Code, Codex or another agent: it reads [agent.md](public/agent.md), sketches what you described, and replies with such a link. - **Projects** – keep as many designs as you like. Each is a project in your browser, and a page lists them all: open, rename, duplicate, save as a file or delete one, and add one from a JSON file or a link. A link you open becomes a project of its own instead of replacing your canvas. **Export all** writes every project into one file, and opening that file brings the list back in any browser. - **MCP** – connect the [`m3e-canvas`](packages/mcp) MCP server to Claude Code, Codex or another MCP client, and your agent designs the screens itself and hands back the link that opens them, or a JSON file for a very large design: `claude mcp add m3e-canvas -- npx -y m3e-canvas` (on Windows, `cmd /c npx …`). Give it the link of a design you finished, and it gets the prompt this app writes and builds the app from it. It runs on your machine and sends nothing anywhere. - **Everything else** – alignment guides and a 4dp grid, undo and redo, keyboard shortcuts, a keyboard-usable parts panel, favorites, install as an app, and autosave in your browser. - **On a phone** – one fixed screen and a buttons-only editor with bottom sheets. The full editor is for desktop browsers.
## Keyboard | Key | Action | | --- | --- | | `V` / `H` | Select / hand tool (hold `Space` to pan) | | Wheel, `Ctrl` + wheel | Pan, zoom | | `+` `-` `0` | Zoom in, zoom out, fit | | `Ctrl+Z` / `Ctrl+Shift+Z` | Undo / redo | | `Ctrl+C` / `Ctrl+V` | Copy / paste parts, also across screens | | `Ctrl+D` | Duplicate | | `Ctrl+G` / `Ctrl+Shift+G` | Group / ungroup | | `Shift` + click | Add to the selection | | Arrows (`Shift` = 8dp) | Nudge | | `Ctrl` + drag | Move without snapping (no guides, no 4dp grid) | | `Delete` | Delete part or screen | | `P` | Preview | ## Run it locally ```bash npm install npm run dev # http://localhost:3000 npm run build # static export to ./out ``` The app is a static Next.js export. To host it under a sub-path (for example a GitHub Pages project site), set `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH=/your-repo` at build time. `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` does this and publishes `out/` to GitHub Pages on every push to `main`. ## Contributing Bug reports, part requests and pull requests are welcome. [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) explains the setup, the conventions (English comments, four languages for every string) and where each kind of change lives. Questions go to [Discussions](https://github.com/lnkiai/m3e-canvas/discussions). ## Support M3E Canvas is free and MIT-licensed, and stays that way. If it saves you time, you can [sponsor the work on GitHub](https://github.com/sponsors/lnkiai); it pays for the hours that go into new parts, the prompt, and reviewing contributions. No feature is behind sponsorship.
